parts.title: Historian Hysteria
parts.summary: Reconcile two equal-length columns of integer location IDs by sorting each list independently in ascending order, pairing elements by rank, and summing the absolute differences across all pairs.
parts.algorithmSummary: Typed-array numeric sort & linear zip: copy left and right columns from immutable LocationLists into private Float64Arrays, call native numeric .sort(), and sum |L[i] - R[i]| with safe-integer overflow validation; differentially verified against a 1D Wasserstein CDF sweep oracle.
parts.complexity: O(N log N) time, O(N) space
learnings: Preserving raw unsorted left and right columns in 2024/day01/shared/LocationLists keeps Part 2 frequency similarity zero-churn.
Sorting private Float64Array copies avoids JavaScript's lexicographic Array.prototype.sort() footgun while covering all safe integers.
A 1D Wasserstein CDF sweep over net multiplicities provides a completely independent differential test oracle for rank-paired distances.

parts.title: Historian Hysteria
parts.summary: Compute the similarity score between the two location ID columns by multiplying each left-column ID by its frequency in the right column and summing across all left-column entries.
parts.algorithmSummary: Right-column hash frequency map with exact BigInt accumulation: count right-column multiplicities in one O(N) pass, then scan raw left entries accumulating BigInt(id) * BigInt(rightCount) with zero churn to 2024/day01/shared; differentially verified against a sorted two-pointer merge oracle.
learnings: Converting operands to BigInt before multiplying (BigInt(id) * BigInt(count)) prevents silent IEEE-754 overflow on arbitrary safe-integer inputs.
Scaling BigInt coordinates in BigInt ((val - min) * 1_000_000n / span) before Number conversion keeps SVG score curves exact across huge ranges.

parts.title: Red-Nosed Reports
parts.summary: Count how many reactor level reports are strictly monotonic (all ascending or all descending) with every adjacent difference between 1 and 3 inclusive.
parts.algorithmSummary: Single-pass directional scan on immutable Report entities in 2024/day02/shared/: derive trend on pair 0 and short-circuit on the first StepFailure (flat, reversal, or jump), differentially verified against a delta-range envelope oracle across 1,000 synthetic reports.
parts.complexity: O(N * L) time, O(1) auxiliary space
learnings: Separating TrendDirection (1 | -1) from flat pair 0 (trend === null) and scanning from index 0 cleanly catches flat starts and initial jumps while leaving isSafeStep reusable for Part 2 bridged checks.
Computing delta, length, trend, and isSafe dynamically on frozen StepFailure and Report value objects eliminates derived-state drift.

parts.title: Red-Nosed Reports
parts.summary: Apply the Problem Dampener allowing at most one level to be omitted from each report, and count how many reports are natively safe or become strictly safe after deleting a single level.
parts.algorithmSummary: Localized first-failure candidate probe reusing 2024/day02/shared with zero churn: if Report.firstFailure() occurs at index k, test minimal ascending skip candidates ([0, 1, 2] when k === 1 to catch index-0 trend flips, else [k, k + 1]) in O(N * L) time and O(1) auxiliary space; differentially verified against an exhaustive O(N * L^2) brute-force oracle across 1,000 reports.
parts.complexity: O(N * L) time, O(1) auxiliary space
learnings: When Report.firstFailure() triggers at index k === 1, removing index 0 can reverse the inferred initial trend and rescue the report; probing [0, 1, 2] for k === 1 and [k, k + 1] otherwise is provably exact and minimal.
Modeling DampenerOutcome as a discriminated union makes inconsistent states (such as unsafe with a removedIndex) compile-time impossible.

parts.title: Mull It Over
parts.summary: Scan a continuous corrupted program memory stream for exact mul(X,Y) calls with 1-to-3-digit unsigned integer operands, ignore all malformed fragments, and sum all valid products.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-backtracking single-pass charCodeAt lexer in 2024/day03/shared/ tokenizing mul(X,Y), do(), and don't() into a frozen ParsedMemory stream in O(N) time; differentially verified against a global RegExp matchAll oracle over adversarial nested prefixes and a 20 KB synthetic corpus.
learnings: Returning the exact mismatch cursor c (not c + 1) in a charCodeAt lexer preserves inner starts of nested prefixes like mul(mul(2,3)) and don'tdon't() with zero backtracking.
Scanning raw memory continuously without line splitting and tokenizing do()/don't() up front keeps Part 2 conditional execution zero-churn.
